title: Limiting coordinates from successive corrections and exact quadratic evaluation
statement: Let $F$ be a field, $S=F[[u,v]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], and $\mathfrak p=(u,v)$. Let $(x_r,y_r)_{r\ge2}$ be a sequence in $S^2$ satisfying $x_2-u,y_2-v\in\mathfrak p^2$ and $x_{r+1}-x_r,y_{r+1}-y_r\in\mathfrak p^r$ for every $r\ge2$. There is a unique pair $(x_\infty,y_\infty)\in S^2$ such that $x_\infty-x_r,y_\infty-y_r\in\mathfrak p^r$ for every $r\ge2$. It satisfies $x_\infty-u,y_\infty-v\in\mathfrak p^2$; for a monomial of total degree $d$, its coefficients in $x_r,y_r$ are constant for $r>d$ and equal those in $x_\infty,y_\infty$. There exists an $F$-algebra automorphism $\beta:S\xrightarrow{\sim}S$ with $\beta(u)=x_\infty$ and $\beta(v)=y_\infty$. Both $\beta$ and $\beta^{-1}$ preserve every $\mathfrak p^N$ and are continuous for the topology with neighbourhood basis $\{\mathfrak p^N\}_{N\ge0}$. For any $a,b,c\in F$, put $Q(U,V)=aU^2+bUV+cV^2$. Then $Q(x_r,y_r)-Q(x_\infty,y_\infty)\in\mathfrak p^{r+1}$ for every $r\ge2$. In particular, for every $f\in S$ such that $f-Q(x_r,y_r)\in\mathfrak p^{r+1}$ for all $r\ge2$, one has $f=Q(x_\infty,y_\infty)=\beta(Q(u,v))$. No discriminant or characteristic hypothesis is required.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-combined-ideal-coefficients] with coefficient ring $F$, coefficient ideal $J=0$ and two variables. Since $N-|E|>0$ whenever $|E|<N$, it says that $h\in\mathfrak p^N$ exactly when every coefficient of $h$ of total degree less than $N$ vanishes (also for $N=0$, when the condition is empty). In particular $\bigcap_N\mathfrak p^N=0$, since every coefficient is tested by some $N$. Also [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-variables-complete] gives $\mathfrak p$-adic completeness of $S$: by [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], every compatible family of residues in $S/\mathfrak p^N$ has a unique lift in $S$. These inputs require only a commutative coefficient ring and finitely many variables, so apply to the given field and the pair $u,v$.

proof.text: Fix a monomial $u^iv^j$ of degree $d=i+j$. For every $r\ge2$ with $r>d$, its coefficient in $x_{r+1}-x_r$ and $y_{r+1}-y_r$ is zero by step 1. Finite telescoping therefore makes the coefficients constant over all indices $r\ge2$ with $r>d$. Define $x_\infty,y_\infty$ to have these eventual coefficients, which define series by [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. For fixed $r\ge2$ all coefficients of degree $d<r$ already have their eventual values, so step 1 gives $x_\infty-x_r,y_\infty-y_r\in\mathfrak p^r$. Another pair with these congruences has the same coefficient in every degree (choose $r>\max(d,1)$), proving uniqueness. Taking $r=2$ and adding the initial congruences gives $x_\infty-u,y_\infty-v\in\mathfrak p^2$. Each $x_r,y_r$, as well as the limits, lies in $\mathfrak p$: for a finite index $r$, telescope from $2$ using $\mathfrak p^j\subseteq\mathfrak p^2$ for $j\ge2$.

proof.text:
Use [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-adic-evaluation] with $C=F$, $T=S$, $I=\mathfrak p$, coefficient map the inclusion of constant series and variable images $x_\infty,y_\infty\in\mathfrak p$. Its completeness hypothesis is [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-variables-complete]. It yields an $F$-algebra endomorphism $b:S\to S$ with $b(u)=x_\infty$, $b(v)=y_\infty$; for $h=\sum h_{ij}u^iv^j$ it gives, for every $M\ge1$,
$$b(h)\equiv\sum_{i+j<M}h_{ij}x_\infty^iy_\infty^j\pmod{\mathfrak p^M}.$$
Here its ring homomorphism is an $F$-algebra map precisely because it fixes constant series. We prove its bijectivity in the following finite calculations rather than assuming an inverse function theorem.

proof.text: Write $x_\infty=u+h_1$, $y_\infty=v+h_2$ with $h_1,h_2\in\mathfrak p^2$. For a monomial of positive degree $d=i+j$, expand $(u+h_1)^i(v+h_2)^j-u^iv^j$: every summand replaces at least one of the $d$ degree-one factors by a factor in $\mathfrak p^2$, so belongs to $\mathfrak p^{d+1}$. For degree zero the difference is zero. For $g\in\mathfrak p^k$ its coefficients of degree less than $k$ vanish by step 1. Apply the finite evaluation formula of step 3 with $M=k+1$; the terms of degree $k$ have unchanged degree-$k$ parts and the lower terms vanish. Thus $b(g)-g\in\mathfrak p^{k+1}$ for every $k\ge1$. For $k=0$ the same formula with $M=1$ shows that the constant coefficient is unchanged, hence $b(g)-g\in\mathfrak p$. Consequently the $F$-linear map $D=1-b$ satisfies $D(\mathfrak p^k)\subseteq\mathfrak p^{k+1}$ for every $k\ge0$, and $b$ preserves each $\mathfrak p^k$. No infinite expansion is used here: each congruence comes from a finite truncation.

source.place: Tag 0C49 (lemma-nodal-algebraic), proof of (2) implies (3), passage from successively higher-order corrections to limiting coordinates. Agent-written coefficientwise details and explicit inverse calculation in the specialized ring F[[u,v]].

proof.text:
For $M\ge1$, the maps $b,D$ descend to $F$-linear maps $b_M,D_M$ on $S/\mathfrak p^M$, and $D_M^M=0$ by step 4 applied repeatedly starting at $\mathfrak p^0=S$. Set $T_M=1+D_M+\cdots+D_M^{M-1}$. Finite telescoping gives
$$b_MT_M=(1-D_M)T_M=1-D_M^M=1=T_Mb_M.$$
These are equalities of linear maps; in particular $b_M$ is bijective. Its inverse $T_M$ is an $F$-algebra map: for $a,c$ in the quotient, apply the injective ring map $b_M$ to $T_M(ac)$ and $T_M(a)T_M(c)$ to obtain $ac$ in both cases, and similarly for addition, constants and $1$. For the quotient projection $q_M:S/\mathfrak p^{M+1}\to S/\mathfrak p^M$, the identity $q_MD_{M+1}=D_Mq_M$ gives $q_MT_{M+1}=T_Mq_M$, since its extra summand $D_M^M q_M$ is zero. Thus these explicit inverses are compatible.

proof.text: For $g\in S$, the residues $T_M(g\bmod\mathfrak p^M)$ are compatible by step 5. Completeness in [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-variables-complete], interpreted by [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], gives a unique element $t(g)\in S$ having exactly these residues for all $M\ge1$. Since $b$ preserves $\mathfrak p^M$, the residues of $b(t(g))$ and $t(b(g))$ are respectively $b_MT_M(g\bmod\mathfrak p^M)$ and $T_Mb_M(g\bmod\mathfrak p^M)$, hence both equal $g\bmod\mathfrak p^M$. The zero intersection in step 1 proves $bt=tb=1$. The same comparison of residues, using that each $T_M$ is an $F$-algebra map, proves that $t$ is an $F$-algebra map. Thus $\beta=b$ is the required $F$-algebra automorphism and $\beta^{-1}=t$, with the prescribed images of $u,v$.

proof.text: Fix $N\ge1$ and $g\in\mathfrak p^N$. Each power of $D$ preserves $\mathfrak p^N$, since $D$ raises its exponent, so $T_M$ preserves the image of $\mathfrak p^N$ in $S/\mathfrak p^M$. At $M=N$ that image is zero, giving $t(g)\bmod\mathfrak p^N=T_N(0)=0$. Therefore $t(\mathfrak p^N)\subseteq\mathfrak p^N$; the forward inclusion for $b$ was proved in step 4. In fact both maps take $\mathfrak p^N$ onto itself by their inverse identities. For $N=0$ this just says both maps preserve $S$. For the topology specified in the statement, these inclusions show continuity at zero (take the same exponent $N$ as source neighbourhood), and at any point because both maps are additive: differences of images are the images of differences.

proof.text:
Fix $r\ge2$, and put $\delta=x_r-x_\infty$, $\epsilon=y_r-y_\infty\in\mathfrak p^r$. In the commutative ring $S$ the exact identity is
$$Q(x_r,y_r)-Q(x_\infty,y_\infty)=a\delta(x_r+x_\infty)+b(\delta y_r+x_\infty\epsilon)+c\epsilon(y_r+y_\infty).$$
Every parenthesized linear coordinate factor is in $\mathfrak p$ by step 2, so this belongs to $\mathfrak p^{r+1}$. If $f-Q(x_r,y_r)\in\mathfrak p^{r+1}$ for every $r\ge2$, addition gives $f-Q(x_\infty,y_\infty)\in\mathfrak p^{r+1}$ for every such $r$. Their intersection is zero by step 1 (every coefficient is tested for some $r$), proving equality. Since $\beta$ is an $F$-algebra map with the given variable images, $\beta(au^2+buv+cv^2)=a x_\infty^2+b x_\infty y_\infty+c y_\infty^2$. This proves the final identity, also when some or all of $a,b,c$ vanish and in characteristic $2$, since neither the identity nor any preceding construction divides by a coefficient or by $2$.
